title: Shadow evaluation probes and autonomous rollback actuator for canary/A-B rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent model/config flips surface regressions that only appear on small but important slices (e.g., long-context prompts, API clients with heavy prefix caching). Current canary gates are metric-by-metric and require manual tuning, which slows rollbacks and increases MTTI.

Goal: Build a lightweight, general-purpose "shadow evaluation probe" subsystem that runs mirrored requests through candidate variants and computes a risk-adjusted composite quality signal per cohort. Pair that with an autonomous rollback actuator that can reduce or revert traffic automatically when the composite crosses calibrated thresholds. The system must be conservative by default, auditable, and reversible.

Approach:
- Instrument shadow probes at the routing layer to mirror a configurable percentage of live traffic to candidate variants without affecting user latency.
- Compute per-request evaluation metrics using existing eval harness (BLEU-like, semantic similarity, safety flags, hallucination detectors). Aggregate into a weighted composite score with tunable weights per project.
- Implement slice-aware scoring: define cohorts by length bins, API route, customer tier, and presence of prefix cache to surface targeted regressions.
- Add a short-term drift detector that looks for rapid divergence relative to baseline over a sliding window and applies a penalty to the composite score to prefer fast reaction on sudden regressions.
- Rollback actuator: policy engine that maps composite score + drift signal + customer_impact to actions (scale down candidate traffic, swap to fallback variant, or full rollback). Include cooldown, grace window, and human notification hooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shadow traffic can mirror up to 10% with <1ms median added latency to p99 path.
- Composite score computed in near-real-time (<= 30s aggregation latency) per cohort.
- Automated rollback triggers in staging and an opt-in canary path in prod that has performed correctly in 3 independent experiments.
- Full audit trail for every trigger (input sample, metrics snapshot, policy decision, and action).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace long-term canary evaluation orchestration or full-band A/B statistical testing; it's a safety-first, fast-reaction subsystem for config/model flips.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks: mitigate with multi-metric voting, cooldowns, and a human-verify fallback state.
- Data privacy from mirrored payloads: redact PII and limit stored traces to hashed identifiers; route audit logs through KMS.
- Operational complexity: keep default policy conservative and expose an advanced policy only to platform admins.

Implementation plan:
1) Design probe spec and cohort definitions (this ticket).
2) Routing shim to mirror requests (ENG-45110 dependent).
3) Eval compute worker to score mirrored outputs (reuse eval infra; small adapter).
4) Policy engine and actuator (rollback library + webhook integration with deployment controller).
5) Staged experiments in internal canary -> opt-in prod -> expanded coverage.

Notes: links to the design doc and prototype tests: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Shadow+Eval+Probes (private) and prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1987.
comments: 2026-01-20 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to keep default risk thresholds strict. Assigned routing shim to ENG-45110 and eval worker adapter to ENG-45201. Need hooks in Console for policy visibility.

2026-01-28 - Jordan Lee: Prototype shadow mirror implemented in routing shim; mirrors HTTP headers and request body to a separate queue. Initial perf: +0.4ms median, +0.8ms p95 on staging. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2113
2026-02-05 - Design review (Kira Santoro): Asked for explicit cohort taxonomy and suggested prebuilt cohorts for 'long-context', 'safety-sensitive', and 'high-throughput' routes. Added to spec.
2026-02-15 - Security (Maya Ortiz): Reviewed data retention plan; approved conditional storage with PII redaction and KMS-wrapped logs. Security checklist attached in design doc.

2026-02-20 - Jordan Lee: Eval adapter complete; uses existing eval models and returns a vector of metrics. Aggregator calculates weighted composite; default weights: semantic=0.5, safety=0.3, hallucination=0.2. Tunable per-project via Console.
2026-02-28 - Observability (Ravi Singh): Added dashboards for composite score by cohort and a per-decision audit table. Tracing spans include sample id and policy evaluation path.

2026-03-03 - Experiment run 1 (staging): Shadowed 5% traffic for 24h against recent model flip. Composite diverged by 0.12 on long-context cohort -> actuator chose 'scale down candidate to 1%'. Manual review indicated minor regression in token-level repetition; no rollback required. Learning: widen grace window to 10 minutes.

2026-03-07 - Experiment run 2 (opt-in prod): Policy executed and automatically reverted a canary after composite hit threshold; rollback action took 35s end-to-end including cooldown. Postmortem: improve aggregation latency to hit <=30s.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Updated policy defaults and increased priority for aggregation performance work (follow-up ENG-45600). Preparing RFC for team review next week.
